{{Short description|Japanese theoretical physicist}}
{{Nihongo|'''Yoshio Koide'''|小出 義夫|Koide Yoshio|born May 16, 1942, in [[Kanazawa, Ishikawa]]}} is a Japanese [[theoretical physicist]] specializing in particle physics. He is best known for the [[Koide formula]], a relation among the masses of charged leptons that has attracted attention for its surprising accuracy. While some physicists regard the formula as potentially significant, others consider it to be a [[mathematical coincidence|numerical coincidence]].

==Early life and education==
Koide received a B.Sc. in physics in 1967 from [[Kanazawa University]], followed by an M.Sc. in theoretical elementary particle physics at the same institution later that year. In 1970, he was awarded a Doctor of Science degree from [[Hiroshima University]] for his thesis “On the Two-Body Bound State Problem of Dirac Particles.”<ref name=koidethesis>{{cite journal|title=On the Two-Body Bound State Problem of Dirac Particles|journal=Progress of Theoretical Physics|author=Koide, Y.|year=1968|volume=39|issue=3|pages=817–829|doi=10.1143/PTP.39.817|bibcode = 1968PThPh..39..817K |doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Career==
After working as a [[postdoc]] in the physics department of Hiroshima University and then a postdoc in the applied mathematics department of [[Osaka University]], he became, from 1972 to 1973, a Lecturer in the School of Science and Engineering, [[Kinki University]], Osaka. Koide was Assistant Professor (1973-1977) then Associate Professor (1977-1987) of General Education, Shizuoka Women's University, [[Shizuoka City|Shizuoka]]. From April 1987 to March 2007 he was a Professor of Physics at [[University of Shizuoka]], Shizuoka and then retired as professor emeritus. In 1986 he was a visiting professor at the [[University of Maryland]] and in 2002 a visiting researcher at [[CERN]]. Koide was from April 2007 to March 2009, a guest professor at Research Institute for Higher Education and Practice, [[Osaka University]], then from April 2009 to March 2011 a guest professor and from April 2011 a guest researcher at Osaka University, and from April 2010 a professor, Department of Maskawa Institute, [[Kyoto Sangyo University]], [[Kyoto]].

==Contributions to physics==
In the composite model of [[meson]]s, Koide's thesis demonstrated that a mass <math>m</math> of a composite particle which consists of the rest masses <math>m_1,m_2</math> cannot be lighter than <math>\frac{1}{2} (m_1+m_2)</math> except for the case <math>m_1 = m_2</math> when J<sup>P</sup> is not = 0<sup>'''-'''</sup>. This offered a severe problem for the quark model. (Koide’s work was done before the establishment of [[Quantum chromodynamics|QCD]].)<ref name= "koidethesis"/>

Katuya and Koide predicted that lifetimes of D<sup>±</sup> and D<sup>0</sup> should be considerably different from what was at that time the conventional anticipation tau(D<sup>±</sup>)= tau(D<sup>0</sup>). Their prediction of these lifetimes was the first in the world prior to the experimental observation.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Katuya, M.|author2=Koide, Y.|title=Is the '''20'''-dominance model valid in charm decays, too?|journal=Physical Review D|volume=19|year=1979|issue=9|pages=2631–2634|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.19.2631|bibcode = 1979PhRvD..19.2631K }}</ref>

He published the famous [[Koide formula]] in 1982<ref>{{cite journal|author=Koide, Y.|title=Fermion-boson two-body model of quarks and leptons and cabibbo mixing|journal=Lettere al Nuovo Cimento|year=1982|volume=34|issue=8|pages=201–205|doi=10.1007/BF02817096|s2cid=120885232}}</ref> with a different presentation in 1983.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Y. Koide|year=1983|title=A fermion-boson composite model of quarks and leptons|journal=[[Physics Letters B]]|volume=120 |issue=1–3 |pages=161–165|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(83)90644-5|bibcode = 1983PhLB..120..161K }}</ref>

Originally, Koide's proposed charged [[lepton]] mass formula was based on a composite model of [[quark]]s and leptons. In a 1990 paper, from the standpoint that the charged leptons are elementary, by introducing a scalar [[boson]] with (octet + singlet) of a family symmetry U(3), Koide re-derived the charged lepton mass formula from minimizing conditions for the scalar potential.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Koide, Y.|title=Charged Lepton Mass Sum Rule from U(3)-FAMILY Higgs Potential Model|journal=Modern Physics Letters A|volume=5|issue=28|pages=2319–2323|year=1990|doi=10.1142/S0217732390002663|bibcode = 1990MPLA....5.2319K }}</ref>

In 2009, he related the [[neutrino]] mixing matrix to the up-quark mass matrix.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Koide, Y.|title=Yukawaon model in the quark sector and nearly tribimaximal neutrino mixing|journal=Physics Letters B|year=2009|volume=680|issue=1|pages=76–80|doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2009.08.038|arxiv = 0904.1644 |bibcode = 2009PhLB..680...76K |s2cid=525463}}</ref> Koide and Hiroyuki Nishiura have published articles on a quark and lepton mass matrix model<ref>{{cite journal|author=Koide, Y.|author2=Nishiura, H.|title= Flavon VEV scales in U(3)×U(3)′ model|journal=International Journal of Modern Physics A|year=2017|volume=32|issue=15|doi=10.1142/S0217751X17500853|arxiv=1701.06287|bibcode=2017IJMPA..3250085K|s2cid=119096804}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Koide, Y.|author2=Nishiura, H.|year=2018|title=Parameter-independent quark mass relation in the U(3) × U(3)′ model|journal=Modern Physics Letters A|volume=33|issue=39|doi=10.1142/S0217732318502309|arxiv=1805.07334|bibcode=2018MPLA...3350230K|s2cid=119079768}}</ref> and a neutrino mass matrix model.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Koide, Y.|author2=Nishiura, H.|year=2019|title=Neutrino Mass Matrix Model with Only Three Adjustable Parameters|class=hep-ph|eprint=1911.03411}}</ref>
